issues.t: Sudden loss of power steering assist (recall)
issues.sym: The steering suddenly becomes very heavy while driving, most noticeable at low speeds and when parking. You may hear a whine from the pump first.
issues.why: The electric-hydraulic power steering pump on these Mazda5s can cut out. Mazda recalled them and replaced the pump and lines. This was the most-reported safety complaint on the 2008 model.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall. If the steering goes heavy, slow down, grip the wheel firmly and drive carefully to a shop.

issues.t: Corroded fuel pump connector can stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls while driving and won't restart, or it cranks but won't start.
issues.why: Water can sit in the fuel pump wiring connector and corrode a pin until it breaks, cutting power to the pump. Mazda recalled 2009-2010 Mazda5s to inspect and replace the connector.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. If the van stalls, get safely off the road and have it towed.

issues.t: Sliding door latch can freeze and not latch (recall)
issues.sym: In freezing weather a sliding door won't latch shut, or it seems closed but isn't fully latched.
issues.why: Water can get into the sliding door latches and freeze. A door that doesn't latch could open while driving. Mazda replaced the latches with a modified design in cold-weather states.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. Always make sure the sliding doors are fully closed and the door-ajar light is off, and use child locks.

issues.t: Liftgate struts can corrode and let the hatch fall (recall)
issues.sym: The rear liftgate doesn't stay up, drifts down, or drops suddenly.
issues.why: The gas struts that hold the liftgate open can corrode and break. Mazda recalled 2012-2015 Mazda5s and other models to replace both struts.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall. Until it's fixed, hold or prop the hatch and keep people clear of it.

issues.t: Worn front struts and control arms
issues.sym: Clunks or knocks over bumps, a bouncy or floaty ride, uneven tire wear, or vague steering.
issues.why: Front struts and control arm bushings wear out on the Mazda5, and suspension is the most-complained-about area for the model. Owners of 2006-2008 vans report worn shocks and loud squeaks from underneath.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected. Replace struts in pairs and get an alignment afterwards so the new tires don't wear out early.

issues.t: Rear shock leaks or broken top mount rattles
issues.sym: A loud rattle or knocking from the rear over bumps, and oily rear shocks.
issues.why: The rear shock absorbers can leak, or the rubber top mount can break and let the shock knock.
issues.next: Have the rear shocks inspected. If only the mount is broken, a separate mount can be fitted; otherwise replace the shocks in pairs.

issues.t: Front sway bar bushings rattle
issues.sym: A rattle or clunk from the front suspension over small bumps or rough pavement.
issues.why: The rubber bushings that hold the front anti-roll bar wear out and let the bar move.
issues.next: Have the bushings and end links checked. They are cheap parts and quick to replace.

issues.t: Uneven or fast tire wear
issues.sym: Tires wear out early or unevenly, sometimes with a rhythmic rumbling noise and cupped tread. Some owners report the van pulling after rotating tires.
issues.why: Owners of 2006-2008 Mazda5s report tires wearing out in as little as 20,000 miles. Worn suspension parts and infrequent tire rotation make it worse.
issues.next: Rotate the tires on schedule, check alignment, and have the struts and bushings inspected if wear keeps returning.

issues.t: Worn top engine mount
issues.sym: More vibration felt in the cabin at idle, especially in Drive, or a thump when pulling away.
issues.why: The upper engine mount wears out and stops absorbing engine movement.
issues.next: Have the mounts checked. Replacing the top mount is a fairly quick job.

issues.t: Automatic transmission failure
issues.sym: Slipping, harsh or delayed shifts, flaring revs, or the van won't move in some gears. Failures are usually at high mileage.
issues.why: Owners of first-generation Mazda5s report automatic transmission failures, with an average around 140,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. If it is slipping, have it diagnosed before it fails completely; a used or rebuilt transmission is usually the fix.

issues.t: Jerky shifting from a failed transmission control module
issues.sym: Harsh, jerky shifts and the automatic transmission (AT) warning light flashes or stays on.
issues.why: The transmission control module, which sits on the transmission under the battery, can fail.
issues.next: Have the codes read. If the module is bad, use the correct part number for your van; rebuilt units vary in quality.

issues.t: Manual clutch slips or wears out early
issues.sym: On manual-transmission vans the engine revs climb without the van speeding up, especially in higher gears, or the clutch pedal feels different.
issues.why: Owners report clutches slipping or failing around 55,000 miles on both generations.
issues.next: Have the clutch checked. Once it slips, replacement is the only fix; a slave cylinder problem should be ruled out first.

issues.t: Starts in Neutral but not in Park
issues.sym: The engine won't crank with the shifter in Park but starts in Neutral.
issues.why: Rust at the pivot of the shift cable stops the transmission from fully reaching the Park position the starter switch looks for.
issues.next: Have the shift cable pivot cleaned and lubricated. Always set the parking brake if you have to start in Neutral.

issues.t: Rust on body panels
issues.sym: Bubbling paint and rust on the body, especially around wheel arches and lower panels, in salt-belt states.
issues.why: First-generation Mazda5s are prone to rust in areas where roads are salted.
issues.next: Wash the underside in winter and treat rust spots early. Have a shop check structural areas before buying an older van.

issues.t: A/C stops cooling from a failed compressor clutch
issues.sym: The A/C blows warm air, and the compressor clutch at the front of the engine doesn't engage.
issues.why: The electric clutch on the A/C compressor fails on many first-generation Mazda5s.
issues.next: Have the A/C diagnosed. Sometimes only the clutch needs replacing, which costs much less than a full compressor.

issues.t: Check engine light from a stuck-open thermostat
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, the engine takes a long time to warm up and the heater is weak.
issues.why: The thermostat can stick open, so the engine runs too cool.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Replacing the thermostat is a modest job and restores heat and fuel economy.

issues.t: Burns oil at higher mileage
issues.sym: The oil level drops between changes even though there is no visible leak. Heavy oil burners may puff bluish smoke.
issues.why: Both the 2.3L and 2.5L engines can start using oil as they age. Separately, some owners of 2006 vans report complete engine failure at high mileage, and running an engine low on oil is a common way to cause that.
issues.next: Check the oil at every fill-up or at least monthly and top it up. Running it low can ruin the engine.

issues.t: Bluetooth module drains the battery
issues.sym: The battery is dead after the van sits overnight.
issues.why: The factory Bluetooth module, behind the glovebox, can fail and keep drawing power.
issues.next: Have a shop do a battery drain test. If the Bluetooth module is the cause, unplug or replace it.

issues.t: Third brake light stops working
issues.sym: The center high-mounted brake light doesn't light up.
issues.why: The wiring connector for the high-mounted brake light can corrode at higher mileage.
issues.next: Have the connector checked. Sometimes it has to be replaced along with the LED light assembly.

issues.t: Check engine light from a leaking EVAP vent valve
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with an evaporative emissions leak code. You may notice no other symptoms.
issues.why: The vent valve in the fuel vapor system can leak.
issues.next: Check that the gas cap is tight first. If the light returns, the vent valve is an inexpensive part to replace.

issues.t: Brief ticking noise on start-up
issues.sym: A short ticking or rattling noise from the engine right after starting, then it goes away.
issues.why: Mazda issued a bulletin for start-up ticking from the variable valve timing system on the 2.3L engine.
issues.next: Use the correct oil and keep it changed. Have a dealer check if the noise lasts longer or gets louder.

issues.t: Sliding door lock hard to operate
issues.sym: The sliding door lock or handle is stiff and hard to work.
issues.why: Mazda issued a service bulletin for sliding door locks that are hard to operate.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check the door against the bulletin. Lubricating the latch and lock mechanism often helps.

issues.t: Fuel pump nozzle clicks off and tank is hard to fill
issues.sym: The gas pump nozzle keeps shutting off early, making the tank slow to fill.
issues.why: A non-return valve in the filler pipe can stick, according to a Mazda service bulletin.
issues.next: Have a dealer check the filler pipe valve. Don't overfill by topping off.
